text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: autoscaler safety-stop triggered in us-west-2 for cluster `inference-prod`. maxNodeCount reached, cluster-autoscaler paused. Observed sustained pod Pending on daemonset/gpu-scheduler and queue growth on `gpu-request-queue` since 03:12 UTC. Paging on-call.

olivia: on it, tailing HPA/autoscaler logs. Queue length ~5200 and rising, most are short inference jobs. Realtime routes showing 95th latency spike (~3.8s -> 12s). Customer impact: degraded throughput for standard tier only; premium routes still fine (pinned nodes).

samir: confirmed ASA (autoscaler) logs show repeated "scale_up forbidden: reached max node count" and safety-stop flag set by policy `scale_safety_stop=true`. Also seeing API throttling 429s from internal enqueue service when the queue hit ~4k.

maya: possible quick mitigations: 1) drain low-priority batch pods to free GPUs, 2) move non-prod workloads to a separate pool, 3) temporary increase node limit with cloud ops. What's the least disruptive?

olivia: prefer draining batch. Which deployments are spiking? `batch-renderer`, `eval-jobs`. I can cordon nodes that run non-critical pools and evict those pods. Will start with annotation to evict by priority: `kubectl -n prod get pods -l workload=batch -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}\n{end}'` then delete with grace 30s.

jon: if we evict, some jobs will restart and requeue — careful with retry loops. Suggest setting `replicas=0` for `batch-renderer` temporarily and add an `ingress` rule to reject new batch submissions. I can patch deploy quickly:

```
kubectl -n prod scale deploy/batch-renderer --replicas=0
kubectl -n prod annotate deploy/batch-renderer redwood/paused=true
```

maya: good. That should free a few GPUs in under 2min. Also we can set a temporary admission webhook deny for jobs with label `priority=low` but that's heavier.

eva-cs: flagging to CS — a handful of power-user tenants reported noisy failures. Sending note: "We are mitigating capacity issue; some standard-tier requests may be delayed. No data loss expected."

samir: I'm applying quick filters on the queue router to throttle background retries (backoff *= 2) so enqueue rate slows and prevents immediate re-surge. Patching now.

olivia: batch-renderer scaled to 0, seeing ~8 GPUs free within 90s. PodPending count dropped from 420 -> 140. Queue growth slowed but still at ~3.2k. 95th latency reduced to ~6.5s.

ops-bot: system: cluster-autoscaler still blocked by maxNodeCount; cloud quota at account-level is 120 nodes. Current desired=120, actual=120.

jon: cloud ops—@samir can you try a temporary node limit bump? If we increase to 140 we should clear backlog, but need authorization. Who can approve?

samir: I can request quota bump via console, but for quick action we can use an emergency policy to allow up to +20 nodes for 2 hours. Need infra lead approval (olivia?).

olivia: I approve temporary bump to 140 for 2 hours. Make sure to schedule automated rollback.

samir: executing resize through cloud API now. Command: 

```
# aws autoscaling example (managed by infra ops)
aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name rg-inference-prod-asg --desired-capacity 140 --honor-cooldown
```

samir: issued change; cloud reports scaling activity accepted. Watching node join events.

maya: in parallel, I pushed a short-lived policy to route all low-priority routes to a fallback small LLM variant to preserve latency for high-priority requests. It's a config flip in routing: `route:set variant=lite for tag=standard-lowprio`

olivia: nodes are coming up. New nodes: +18, kube join ok, pods scheduling. Pending pods now 30. Queue drained from 3.2k -> 900 in ~4 min. 95th latency back to 2.0s.

eva-cs: sending customer update: "We scaled capacity to restore normal performance; backlog is clearing and latency is improving. We'll follow up with root cause." :white_check_mark:

jon: reminder: need rollback and postmortem action items — why did safety-stop flip on? Possibly misconfigured scale policy + a burst of eval jobs from staging hitting prod resource pool. Recommend: stricter namespace resource quotas, move staging to isolated cluster, and automatic traffic shed for low-priority routes during surge.

samir: logging the temporary node increase as incident action item. I'll set automated rollback at UTC+2h: scale group will be set back to 120 with a safe drain procedure.

olivia: agreed. I'll start an incident runbook doc and capture timelines. Quick notes:
- Trigger: autoscaler safety-stop at 03:12 UTC when desired==maxNodes
- Impact: queue growth, standard-tier latency spike, ~10% error rate on enqueue
- Mitigations: scaled down batch-renderer, throttled queue router, temporary node bump (+20), routing variant fallback
- Owner: olivia (incident lead), samir (infra ops), maya (runtime)

ops-bot: incident status changed -> mitigated. Postmortem requested :clipboard:

olivia: assigning postmortem. I'll include logs, autoscaler config, and a proposal to implement an automated low-priority shed policy. Anyone want co-auth?

maya: I'll co-author and add suggested admission webhook to prevent staging jobs from running in prod.

eva-cs: will follow up with affected customers and include support ticket IDs.

samir: scheduling a follow-up runbook review tomorrow 16:00 UTC. Closing thread once postmortem is filed. :pray:
